I did not look up any benchmark data; these probabilities come from rough priors about NAS-Bench-201, not from computation or lookups.

- **Replacing a weak operation (3, 19):** I rated these high. When the condition says the edge currently holds a weak op (avg_pool or none), the edit's gain is larger than when the edge holds something stronger.
- **Replacing a strong operation (7, 11, 17, 25):** I rated these very low. When the condition says the edge currently holds a conv op, swapping it for a weaker one hurts more than the average case.
- **Redundant paths (1, 10):** I rated these low. If another path already carries the signal, an edit has less effect.
- **Weak alternatives (2, 23, 29):** I rated these slightly above the baseline. If a competing path is absent, an edit may matter more.
- **Everything else:** I left these near the baseline because I have no strong reason to expect an interaction.
